summary.text: 真 commonly means ‘true,’ ‘actual,’ or ‘genuine.’ One proposal says the graph was reused to write ‘true’ because an earlier word sounded alike, though that word and sound match remain unidentified. A reported Western Zhou bronze personal-name use does not identify the name’s spoken form or meaning.

formation.text: The bronze graph has competing analyses. One treats 𠂈 as phonetic and 貝 as semantic; some forms are described with 鼎 in place of 貝, and one adds 丌 of unidentified role. Another proposal takes 真 as an early graph for 珍, ‘precious.’ A separate account says 真 was reused to write ‘true’ because the words may have sounded alike. The earlier word and sound match are unknown, so this borrowing mechanism is proposed rather than demonstrated; the graph’s origin remains unresolved.

components.text: One analysis identifies 𠂈 as a phonetic element in the bronze graph. It is proposed to cue pronunciation, but the available evidence does not establish its historical sound relation to 真.

sound_limitation.text: The available readings provide a modern comparison, but no historical component-to-host sound comparison. The modern pair does not establish the proposed ancient phonetic relation.

sound.text: These modern readings differ and do not establish the proposed ancient sound relation.

components.text: In one analysis of the bronze graph, 貝 (‘cowry shell’) is semantic, though its specific contribution to the proposed early meaning is not identified.
Some descriptions identify 鼎 in forms where others identify 貝, reporting that the graphs could be confused. 鼎’s role in 真 is not established.
One described form on 真盤 adds 丌 below the other elements. Its role is not identified.

In the received Shuowen analysis of 眞, 目 is parsed with 𠤎, 乚, and 八 as part of an interpretation about an immortal transforming and ascending to heaven. This later philological account does not establish the bronze graph’s original referent.
Shuowen parses 𠤎 with 目, 乚, and 八 in its account of 眞; this does not establish the bronze graph’s original referent.
乚 is included in Shuowen’s interpretation of 眞; its independent function is not identified.
八 is included in Shuowen’s interpretation of 眞; its independent function is not identified.

history.text: The cited accounts report Western Zhou bronze attestations, including a personal-name use. Descriptions include forms with 貝 and 𠂈, forms identified with 鼎, and one form with an added 丌. These accounts do not settle what the graph represented.

Later descriptions trace graphic changes, including 貝 becoming 目-like in Spring and Autumn forms and further changes in the Warring States period. The received seal-script graph 眞 has a separate traditional analysis through 𠤎, 目, 乚, and 八.
The modern standard 真 has an upper portion written like 直, while the received seal-script graph is 眞. The cited accounts describe these forms but do not specify every step connecting them.

uncertainties.text: The bronze personal-name use does not identify the spoken word or meaning. Proposals connect the early graph with 珍 (‘precious’), with 殄 or 顛, or with a later use for ‘true’; the lexical origin remains unresolved.
For the proposed borrowing of the graph to write ‘true,’ the earlier word and its sound resemblance to the later word remain unknown. The sound-based mechanism is proposed, not demonstrated.
Shuowen’s interpretation of 眞 as an immortal transforming and ascending to heaven is a historical philological account, not direct evidence for the bronze graph’s referent or earliest meaning.

senses.period: Qin Shuihudi legal-question bamboo manuscript cited for slip 49; exact manuscript and composition dating unresolved
senses.text: A cited legal discussion uses 真 to mean ‘actual’ or ‘true.’ The bronze personal-name use does not identify its spoken sense or establish this meaning for that use.

senses.period: Texts cited from Zhuangzi and Lüshi Chunqiu; exact composition and witness dates unresolved
senses.text: 真 is cited in uses meaning ‘original nature’ or ‘inherent nature.’ Their chronology relative to the ‘true/actual’ use is not established.

senses.period: Text cited from Xunzi; exact date and witness relation unresolved
senses.text: 真 is cited as an adverb meaning ‘indeed.’ Its chronology relative to the other cited senses is not established.
Modern definitions include ‘real,’ ‘actual,’ ‘true,’ and ‘genuine.’ The supplied evidence does not trace a complete path from the cited early uses to these current meanings.

developments.text: Both uses are attested, but their relationship and chronology are not established.
The adverbial use is separately attested; its development from ‘true/actual’ is not established.
‘Genuine’ is a current meaning, but the evidence does not establish its historical path from the cited ‘true/actual’ use.

limitations.text: The reported bronze personal-name use does not establish that 真 originally meant ‘true’; it does not reveal the name’s spoken word or meaning.
The evidence does not establish a complete chronology among ‘true/actual,’ ‘inherent nature,’ and ‘indeed,’ or how the cited uses led to current meanings.

overview.text: 真 commonly means ‘true’ or ‘real.’ One proposal says the graph was reused for ‘true’ because an earlier word sounded alike, though that word and sound match remain unidentified. A reported Western Zhou bronze personal-name use has an unknown spoken form and meaning.

components.text: In Modern Mandarin, 𠂈 is read jié and 真 zhēn; this difference does not establish the proposed ancient sound relation.
One account gives 貝 a meaning role in the early graph, but its specific contribution is unclear.
Some descriptions identify 鼎 in certain forms and 貝 in others; 鼎’s role remains unresolved.
One described bronze form adds 丌 below; its role is not identified.
In Shuowen’s later analysis of 眞, 目 belongs to an interpretation distinct from the bronze analyses.
Shuowen also parses 𠤎 as part of its interpretation of 眞; this does not explain the bronze graph’s origin.
乚 appears in Shuowen’s later analysis of 眞; its independent role is not identified.
八 appears in the same later analysis of 眞, not as an established part of the bronze analysis.

relationships.text: One analysis identifies 𠂈 as a phonetic element in the bronze graph. The available modern reading pair, 𠂈 jié and 真 zhēn, does not establish that proposed ancient role.
One analysis treats 貝 as semantic alongside phonetic 𠂈; competing accounts of the early graph remain unresolved.
Some descriptions identify 鼎 where others identify 貝, but the reported graphic confusion does not establish 鼎 as a depicted object contributing meaning to 真.
The received seal-script form is 眞 and the modern standard graph is 真. The cited accounts describe their graphic difference but do not specify every step between them.
